title: Large Language Models for Emphysema Board Decision Making
summary:
Background

In the treatment of lung diseases such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and emphysema, computer programs with artificial intelligence (AI) are already helping to better understand X-ray or CT images, predict disease progression, and evaluate reports more quickly.

Research Question
However, there are currently few studies that examine whether such AIs can make decisions as accurately as a real team of physicians from various specialties (the so-called emphysema board) when faced with truly difficult treatment decisions (for example, whether surgery, small valves in the lungs, or medication alone are the best option).

Methodology
In this study, we retrospectively examine 50 real patient cases from recent years. We provide the AI ​​with the exact same anonymized information (e.g., lung function values, lung images, and comorbidities) that the medical team had at the time. We then compare: Does the AI's treatment recommendation match the medical team's actual decision? The aim is to determine how closely the AI ​​already matches the experts' assessments and where it still needs improvement.
conditions: Severe pulmonary emphysema in COPD patients with a focus on therapeutic decisions regarding interventional lung procedures.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of therapeutic agreement between computer-generated suggestions and multidisciplinary board decisions in patients with COPD and pulmonary emphysema from 2021 to 2026

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Data analysis of patients who were in treatment between 2021 and 2026
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion of all cases without a full board decision, without sufficient HRCT findings, without lung function data, or with incomplete documentation of the relevant routine data.
